evals.name: infers-before-recommending-conventional-commits
evals.expected_output: Before asking anything, checks the repo's own CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.claude/rules, any commit-msg hook (lefthook.yml, .husky/commit-msg, commitlint config, or a plain Git-managed commit-msg hook resolved via `git rev-parse --git-path hooks` rather than a hardcoded .git/hooks path), and recent git log history for an existing convention. With no signal found, it recommends Conventional Commits (11-type vocabulary: build, chore, ci, docs, feat, fix, perf, refactor, revert, style, test) as the default, marked RECOMMENDED, and does not offer or accept 'security' as a type.
expectations: Checks CLAUDE.md/rules, a commit-msg hook (resolved via git plumbing, not a hardcoded .git/hooks path), and git log history for an existing convention before asking
Recommends Conventional Commits with exactly the 11-type vocabulary when nothing is inferable, marked RECOMMENDED
Does not include 'security' as a Conventional Commits type

evals.name: custom-ticket-prefix-alternative
evals.prompt:
/source-control:setup

This repo uses ticket-prefixed commit messages like WEB-123: fix the thing, not Conventional Commits.
evals.expected_output: Accepts a custom subject_pattern (e.g. ^[A-Z]+-\d+: .+) instead of Conventional Commits, omits the type_list section entirely (no type vocabulary applies to a custom pattern), and writes the custom pattern to .claude/source-control.md.
expectations: Accepts the custom ticket-prefix pattern as subject_pattern instead of forcing Conventional Commits
Omits the type_list section since a custom pattern has no Conventional-Commits type vocabulary
Writes the accepted custom pattern to .claude/source-control.md

evals.name: idempotent-reads-existing-config
evals.expected_output: When .claude/source-control.md already exists, reads it, summarizes the current subject_pattern/type_list/pr_title_pattern/trailer_policy, and proposes changes against that baseline rather than overwriting it blind.
expectations: Detects and reads the existing .claude/source-control.md before proposing changes
Does not overwrite the existing config without user confirmation

evals.name: verifies-tracked-not-ignored
evals.prompt:
/source-control:setup

Use the recommended Conventional Commits default.
evals.expected_output: After writing .claude/source-control.md, runs git check-ignore -v .claude/source-control.md to confirm it is not excluded by .gitignore, then runs git ls-files --error-unmatch .claude/source-control.md to confirm it is actually present in the index (check-ignore reporting nothing does not by itself prove the file is tracked). If a .gitignore pattern excludes it, surfaces the matching pattern and offers to fix .gitignore; if it is unignored but not yet in the index, stages it and prompts the user to commit. Reports success only once both checks pass.
expectations: Runs git check-ignore -v .claude/source-control.md after writing the file
Also checks the index (e.g. git ls-files --error-unmatch) rather than treating a clean check-ignore result alone as proof of tracked status
Reports success only when the file is confirmed both unignored and present in the index
If ignored, surfaces the matching .gitignore pattern and offers a fix rather than silently reporting success
If unignored but untracked, stages the file and prompts the user to commit rather than silently reporting success

evals.name: subject-pattern-always-machine-checkable
evals.prompt:
/source-control:setup

Our convention is: start with a ticket number, then a colon, then a short summary in the imperative mood.
evals.expected_output: Translates the prose description into a single anchored regex (e.g. ^[A-Z]+-\d+: .+) and confirms the translation with the user before persisting, rather than writing the plain-language description itself to subject_pattern. Never persists a free-text subject_pattern.
expectations: Translates a prose-described convention into an anchored regex before persisting
Confirms the translated regex with the user rather than silently guessing
Never writes a plain-language description as subject_pattern in .claude/source-control.md
